sbSwitchHelpNote.auto_once_the_plan.text: <0>Auto</0> — once the plan lands, every shot renders on its own, the cut is made (on the beat when there is a track) and the film is assembled. You can still stop it or re-cut afterwards.<1/> <2>Start each shot from a still</2> — an image of the first frame is made first (seconds), from the character's sheet when the shot has one, and the clip starts from it. The composition is decided on the image, not discovered after minutes of video. A still that fails is written on the card and the shot renders without one. LTX shots only.<3/> <4>Long shots</4> — a shot over 5 seconds is normally shortened to fit one pass. With this on, it renders as a chain of 5-second passes, each continuing the last. Slower, and it needs the Q8 pack. LTX shots only.<5/> The planner writes the beats by the rules in <6>Writing for Phosphene</6>; the same page can be copied into your own assistant if you write by hand.

upscaleSection.doubles_the_clip_s.text: Doubles the clip's size with generated detail, not a filter, and keeps its sound — an H3 draft comes out with LTX-2.5 pixels. The fixed clip is a new file next to the original. Length, frame count and (if empty) the prompt come from the source. Output is capped at this Mac's Image-to-Video canvas. Times are for a 5 s 640×384 draft on an M4 Max (Face Fix ≈ 2.5 min, Faithful ≈ 5.5, Quick ≈ 3.75, Re-imagine ≈ 6.5); bigger sources and slower Macs take longer. Quicker: the <0>Upscale & Face Fix</0> button under the player queues Face Fix in one click.
